thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency breach on /v1/stream-gen (us-west-2) — p99=1.8s, p95=450ms, increased streaming stalls. ECC correctable errors rising on gpu-node gpu-45. Paging on-call. https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/3850012345

alice_oncall: ack — I’m on it. pulling traces & will coordinate mitigation. @bob_sre @carol_runtime

bob_sre: on it. seeing ECC correctables spiking on gpu-45 over last 6m. Prom query:
```
sum(rate(node_gpu_ecc_correctable_total{node=\"gpu-45\"}[5m])) by (node)
```
node shows ~480/min, others < 5/min. Also thermal sensors show rising case temp and fan ramp.

carol_runtime: streaming tail p99 aligns with GPU stalls — KV cache misses spike for sessions routed to gpu-45. Suggest immediate evacuation of inference workloads off that node, set routing fallback to gpu-44 (same AZ) and reduce concurrency for streaming route.

alice_oncall: agreed. steps: 1) set routing weight gpu-45=0, fallback to gpu-44; 2) decrease streaming concurrency limit to 2 for /v1/stream-gen; 3) drain pods on gpu-45. Starting now.

alice_oncall: applying route tweak:
```
redwoodctl route update --route /v1/stream-gen --set-weight gpu-45=0,gpu-44=1.0
```

alice_oncall: lowering concurrency:
```
redwoodctl config set /v1/stream-gen --concurrency=2 --scope=streaming
```

erin_monitoring: Noted changes, new route weights applied in 12s. Dash: https://dash.redwood.example/streams/overview

bob_sre: preparing drain:
```
kubectl drain gpu-node/gpu-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
starting evacuation of pods (will trigger routing fallback). ETA ~90s for active sessions to failover, streaming may drop for in-flight sessions.

dave_support: any customers impacted yet? I have an open convo with Acme Corp, they use streaming. Need an ETA to update them.

alice_oncall: ping @dave_support — currently degraded p99, we expect routing fallback to restore stable p99 in ~2m, but some in-flight streams might drop. Triage in progress. I'll post customer note after mitigation stable.

carol_runtime: watching streaming buffer metrics. After weight change, tail stalls dropped from 1.8s -> ~600ms in 45s. Good sign. ECC count still elevated; recommend quarantining gpu-45 for hardware inspection.

bob_sre: marking node unschedulable and creating maintenance ticket #INFR-1234. tagging hardware-oncall.

bob_sre: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node/gpu-45
```

bob_sre: maintenance ticket created: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/INFR-1234

alice_oncall: customer note draft:
"We observed elevated latency and streaming disruptions affecting /v1/stream-gen in us-west-2. Mitigation: routed traffic away from a degraded GPU node and reduced concurrency to limit retries. Most customers should see normal service; some in-flight streams experienced drops. Engineering is investigating hardware ECC correctable error spikes."

dave_support: sending to Acme now, will update if they report anything. :thumbsup: 

erin_monitoring: alert suppressor enabled for this incident to avoid noise. p99 now at ~420ms and stable for 2m.

frank_pm: are we trending any SLO breaches overall? what's impact window? if p99 >1.5s for 6m we might need external notification.

alice_oncall: SLO check:
```
# rough check
count_over_time((request_latency_seconds_bucket{le=\"0.99\"})[10m])
```
We breached p99 SLO for ~6m. Classifying as SEV2. I'll file the incident doc.

carol_runtime: post-mitigation: capture kernel logs and ECC counters, dump NVML output from node for hardware team:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv -i 45
```
Also collecting runtime traces: /var/log/redwood/runtime/streams/gpu-45/*.log

bob_sre: grabbing dmesg and i2c sensor logs, pushing to ticket.

alice_oncall: handing off to eng-oncall for next shift. Mitigation complete: traffic routed off node, p99 stable. Leaving notes in incident doc and linking jira. follow-ups: hardware check (INFR-1234), postmortem (SEV2-3850012345).

bob_sre: adding labels: cause:hardware_ecc, mitigation:node_evacuation, impact:streaming_p99_breach

alice_oncall: thanks team. switching status to 'mitigated' and starting the post-incident. If new symptoms reappear ping this thread. :white_check_mark:
